title: Polycarp (c. 155)
hookLine: the old bishop refuses to curse Christ: eighty-six years I have served him

cards: Swear the oath, curse Christ, and I'll let you go. A Roman governor says it in a packed stadium in Smyrna, to a very old man. The crowd is shouting.
The governor presses again and again, and threatens wild beasts, then fire. The old man is Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna. Ignatius once wrote him a letter on the road to Rome.
His answer to the governor is not an argument. It's a number.

teach.b: His answer, in Lightfoot's translation of the Martyrdom of Polycarp: "Fourscore and six years have I been His servant, and He hath done me no wrong. How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?"
Eighty-six years: a life added up. First, the source: a letter from the church of Smyrna to another church, telling what happened to their bishop. Second, the arrest.
When soldiers find him at a farm outside the city, he comes down and talks with them.

teach.h: FOOD FOR THE SOLDIERS, AN HOUR TO PRAY.
teach.b: He has food and drink set out for them, as much as they want, and asks only for an hour to pray.
He prays standing, remembering everyone he has ever met, small and great, for two hours, until some of the soldiers are sorry they came. Third, the stadium.
As he walks in, the account says, a voice comes from heaven: be strong, Polycarp, and play the man.
The governor tells him to respect his age, and to say: away with the atheists. That's what the crowd called Christians, because they wouldn't worship the gods.
Polycarp looks at the crowd, waves his hand toward them, sighs, looks up to heaven, and says it: away with the atheists. He just means a different crowd. Fourth, what his church did next.
They gathered his bones, more precious than jewels, they said, and planned to meet there to keep what they called the birthday of his martyrdom.
The Catholic calendar still marks many saints on the day they died, which it calls their birth into heaven. Polycarp's church turned a death day into a birthday.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Saint Polycarp each year, and the Church's calendar often sets a saint's day on the day of death, called the birth into heaven.

o: an old bishop of Smyrna who would not curse Christ
the governor who judged the Christians at Smyrna
the first bishop of Rome after Peter's death

fed by the man they came to arrest

he came down, fed them, and asked for an hour to pray.
because they would not worship the gods.

games.q: you're Polycarp. soldiers have arrived at the farm to arrest you. it's late. what do you do?
o: slip out the back and hide.
set food before them and ask for an hour to pray.
games.why: he feeds the men who came to arrest him, then prays for two hours, until some are sorry they came.

practice: Say your age to yourself, then let the years go by in chunks: childhood, school, the first job, the move, the loss, the person who changed things.
Don't stop to judge any of it; Polycarp didn't say every year was easy, only that the One he served had done him no wrong.
If you pray, give thanks one stretch at a time; if you don't, notice that you're still here, and what carried you.

wordCard.voice: Polycarp. The old bishop of Smyrna who would not curse Christ after a lifetime of serving him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: witness — the word behind martyr.

carryVoice: Your line: eighty-six years. A lifetime of faithfulness, said in one number. Day seven hundred five.
